questions.q: What does a RACI table make explicit, according to this lesson?
options: Exactly who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for a specific activity, rather than leaving it assumed
The server hosting location for each system
The exact dollar budget for the governance program
A list of every employee at LTV Global
questions.explain: The lesson frames the RACI as turning 'someone should probably handle this' into a specific, named answer for each activity.

questions.q: Who sponsors the data governance program this capstone follows?
options: Dana Whitfield, the newly hired Chief Data Officer
A customer in Leeds
The warehouse management vendor
No one — the program has no sponsor
questions.explain: The board gave newly hired CDO Dana Whitfield the mandate and budget to stand up the program, making her the executive sponsor for this capstone's scenario.

questions.q: Why did Product, Order, and Marketing consent resolve as authoritative-source decisions in a single meeting?
options: Each domain has exactly one system that clearly does that job and no other system duplicates it
Those three domains have no data at all
They were decided randomly without discussion
They required building a golden record, just like Customer
questions.explain: Atlas is the sole system that assigns SKUs and invoices orders, and Beacon is the sole system that captures marketing consent, making each an easy single-source call.

questions.q: What incident does this lesson's retrospective trace the entire program back to?
options: A warehouse inventory mismatch at Harbor
The six-week UK GDPR data subject access request from Lesson 1, which surfaced conflicting order histories and reached the board
A failed Power BI dashboard refresh
An unrelated vendor contract dispute
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly closes the loop back to the Lesson 1 DSAR incident as the origin point for everything the program built.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Lesson 15 within this chapter's arc?
options: To write a brand-new strategy document not based on earlier lessons
To replace the operating model chosen in Lesson 12
To gather everything built across Lessons 1-14 into one numbered, organized deliverables package
To conduct the final retrospective on the whole program
questions.explain: The lesson is explicitly the gathering step, pulling fourteen prior lessons' artifacts into one package before Lesson 16's synthesis writing begins.

questions.q: Why did Customers.Email score high enough to become a CDE?
options: It scored high on regulatory impact and is the exact element behind the Lesson 1 DSAR incident
It is the longest column name in the schema
It has no relationship to any real-world problem
It only matters to the IT department
questions.explain: Email is personal data under UK/California privacy law and was the specific element at the center of the access-request gap from Lesson 1.

questions.q: Why did LTV Global reject a fully decentralized operating model?
options: That is essentially what already existed before the program started, and it's what caused the Lesson 1 incident
Decentralized models are always faster, so it was rejected for being too slow
LTV Global has no business units to decentralize into
It would have required firing the data stewards
questions.explain: The lesson states a fully decentralized model describes the pre-program status quo — three disconnected systems with no one accountable for reconciliation.

questions.q: What is a 'data domain' as used in this lesson's inventory?
options: A logical grouping of related data, such as Customer, Product, or Order
A physical server rack location
A single column in a single table
A company's internet domain name
questions.explain: The Key terms section defines a data domain as a logical grouping of related data, which is how the inventory table organizes each system's contents.

questions.q: What closes out the Success Metrics section, tying the document back to its Executive Summary?
options: A list of unrelated software licensing costs
A disclaimer that no metrics are currently tracked
The same six-week DSAR from the Executive Summary now carries a ten-business-day response target, measured monthly
A request to delete the golden Customer record
questions.explain: The lesson closes Success Metrics by circling back to the DSAR incident from the Executive Summary, now expressed as a measured KPI target from Lesson 11.

questions.q: Which KPI in this lesson is a direct, measured answer to the Lesson 1 incident?
options: Access request response time, targeted at under 10 business days
CDE ownership coverage
Quality check pass rate
None of the KPIs relate to the Lesson 1 incident
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties access request response time back to the six-week DSAR delay from Lesson 1, now tracked against a 10-day target.

questions.q: In the 'VP wants a policy exception' scenario, what does the strong answer avoid doing?
options: Granting the access simply because of the VP's seniority, without routing it through the documented exception process
Logging the request at all
Ever granting any exception under any circumstance
Involving the data owner in the decision
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that seniority alone doesn't justify bypassing the documented, logged exception process and the data owner's sign-off.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does pay and title vary unusually widely for data governance roles compared to some other data roles?
options: Titles aren't standardized, regulated industries tend to fund the role more formally, and the role can sit in different departments (IT, data, or compliance)
Because data governance is not considered a real job by any employer
Because governance roles are always the highest-paid data role at every company
Because governance work requires no specialized skill at all
questions.explain: The lesson lists inconsistent titles, industry regulation intensity, and which department the role reports into as concrete reasons governance pay and scope vary more than some other data roles.

questions.q: What is the signature follow-up question the lesson pairs with a RACI matrix?
options: "Who is the single Accountable role here, and why that person and not someone else?"
"How many colors are used in this diagram?"
"What font was used to create this document?"
"Who typed this document?"
questions.explain: The lesson lists this exact question as the one a RACI matrix needs to survive, tied to the single-A rule from earlier in the path.

questions.q: In the referential integrity check, why does the query include 'AND o.CustomerId IS NOT NULL' alongside 'c.CustomerId IS NULL'?
options: Because a NULL foreign key usually means 'no customer, intentionally,' which is a completeness issue, not an orphaned row
Because SQL Server requires at least two conditions in every WHERE clause
Because it makes the query run in half the time automatically
Because CustomerId can never legally be NULL in any schema
questions.explain: The lesson explains that without this condition, legitimately-NULL foreign keys (like guest checkouts) would be miscounted as orphaned rows.

questions.q: A business user asks you to informally grant them access to a dataset classified as restricted. What does this lesson say is the right response?
options: Follow the documented access request and approval process rather than granting access because someone asked
Grant it immediately since the user already knows the data exists
Refuse to ever discuss access requests with business users
Grant access only if the user is a manager, regardless of role or process
questions.explain: Access decisions for sensitive data follow a documented, role-based approval process. Granting access informally bypasses the control that governance exists to enforce.

questions.q: What four-part structure does the lesson recommend for explaining a long capstone project quickly?
options: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Introduction, Body, Conclusion, Questions
Problem, Budget, Timeline, Invoice
Name, Rank, Serial Number, Date
questions.explain: The lesson's structure is explicitly Situation, Task, Action, Result, in that order.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what typically distinguishes a Data Governance Manager / Lead from a Data Governance Analyst?
options: The manager is usually Accountable at the program level, running the operating model, councils, and KPIs
The manager never interacts with stakeholders
The analyst has final sign-off authority over every domain
There is no real difference between the two titles anywhere
questions.explain: The lesson describes the Governance Manager/Lead role as usually Accountable at the program level, running councils, KPIs, and stakeholder communication.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend using a LinkedIn headline's roughly 220 characters for?
options: Searchable terms and a concrete claim, not just a repeated job title
A full paragraph describing your entire work history
Your phone number and home address
A list of every company you have ever applied to
questions.explain: The lesson specifically warns against wasting the headline on a repeated job title and recommends searchable terms plus a concrete claim.

questions.q: Which three courses make up the "Advanced & Specialized Governance" group in this path, according to this lesson?
options: AI & Machine Learning Governance, Data Governance Program Management, and Data Governance Architecture
Data Quality Management, Metadata Management & Business Glossary, and Data Lineage & Impact Analysis
Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Fabric Data Governance, and Snowflake Data Governance
Power BI Governance, Cloud Data Governance: Azure & AWS, and Data Governance Career & Capstone
questions.explain: The lesson groups AI & Machine Learning Governance, Data Governance Program Management, and Data Governance Architecture together as the path's most senior, specialized territory, directly connecting to the career ladder from Lesson 34.

questions.q: Which lesson in this course does the governance interview landscape lesson point to for direct SQL and data quality practice?
options: Lesson 26
Lesson 1
Lesson 35
There is no such lesson referenced
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states Lesson 26 practices the technical/data quality screen directly.
